newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends firm at day's high but trade slow.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends firm at day's high but trade slow.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures closed slightly firmer at session highs on late short-covering, but volume was thin on Monday.
May ended up one stg at its session high of 1,013 stg per tonne and July gained five to 1,030. Total volume was a lackluster 4,988 contracts.
Light profit-taking and small speculative sales pressured prices in the morning after New York closed well off its session high on Friday, traders said.
But when downward momentum failed to materialise in the afternoon when New York reopened and Friday's lows in May and July held, traders said day speculators covered up early short positions.
That short-covering lifted prices out of negative ground and to session highs just before the close.

Though most funds probably finished liquidating or rolling out of May and into July and further months, floor traders noted some light, last-minute switching. They said the switches looked like funds holding and moving long positions into back months, which kept those months firm against nearby May.
In addition, May's first notice day in New York is on April 17. As of Friday's close, CSCE May open interest notched 9,556 contracts, down 4,021 from the previous day.
Despite Monday's slim gains, traders remained mixed on cocoa's outlook. Some expected prices to rise after a couple of days of consolidation near current levels.
Elliot Wave analysts said chances of a fifth wave up on CSCE July cocoa could push the contract up to about $1,600 to $1,625 per tonne by the third week of May, which would boost London prices.
July resistance here was pegged at 1,035 and support between 980 and 990.
May resistance was seen between 1,015 and the April 2 peak of 1,050. Initial support rests at 1,000 with stronger support between 979 and 980.

Other traders were less optimistic, still wary of the funds after last week's fund-led sell-off that pushed prices down more than five percent. They said funds were still net long and could decide to trim their positions again and cause another sharp drop.
But floor traders said stops on either side of the market were still far from current prices. July sell-stops were pegged closer to 975 and buy-stops between 1,058 and 1,060.
In options, 10 July 1,100 calls traded, according to LIFFE.
